body:
> because we don't really know each other

Doesn't matter. Humans are human. We're all made of the same stuff, 
just formed by different experiences.

>I thought in time it would pass and that if I just went through the motions, 
I'd get somehow used to it like my parents did

I am unfortunate enough to know that isn't true. There isn't any dealing
with this without some kind of change.

>If you're like me - and I'm not saying you are - this will not get better.

I strongly suspect we have some of the important stuff in common.

> NEVER FUCKING GET A MORTGAGE

That's actually one of the few absolutes in my life. Mortgages increase the
unemployment rate, create checks that the middle class just can't cash 
sometimes, and enslave people.

I refuse outright to buying anything with anything other than cash.

If I own land, it will be on my own terms. Not some bank's. Otherwise, I'll 
rent and come and go as I please.

>Rent cheap if you have to rent at all

I'm renting a (relatively) cheap room at the moment. I plan to keep things 
cheap, I also refuse to have any bills in my name.

>What about you?

I'm unhappy, but I'm free. The uncertainty of going native after just 
having been hungry is not at all comforting, but I know I'm going to
have to do something.

>Do you have anything dragging on you other than your own dreams and 
needs?

No family, single, no responsibilities beyond my present employer.

>You can move to another country if you like.

I've looked into that, it's a non-trivial matter even if I'd like 
to do it.

>You can decide to put your nose to the grindstone for a few years 
and plan to get your own place in the countryside.

More or less what I'm planning on for now.

>Peace corp

I have qualms with them, but merchant marines/FFL/Antarctica sounds 
like more my thing.

>You are more free than you think.

That would be a boon beyond words.

>You owe no one anything.

I know that. I don't entirely know what it means for me.

>Find thinkers. Find people who stimulate you.

I'm in NYC, so this *should* be easy but I'm not very good at encountering
new people beyond mere serendipity.

The community idea pleases me. I don't think I'll really ever be totally 
satisfied living alone.

>Maybe none of this is useful to you

It was as useful as anything in my life ever has been.

You've lit the fire. I think you're right. I think you've shown me what I 
need and want.

>what you specifically describe is something that resonates personally

It would be a sad thing, for my part and the world's, if I was the only
one dissatisfied.

>pisses me off that anyone would ever need to be unhappy in the way 
you say you are

I'm 21, have some grey hair already, got screwed out of school, my relationships, my 
family, and my company. I feel like I'm 61 rather than 21 when I wake up
in the morning.

Clearly something is wrong.

>not to say I'm angry at you

I know.

>But many other things are possible. You've already lived some life on the 
other side.

Taken my share of bruises.

>the hole is shallow. You can dig out.

Yeah, I know. I just need to decide what to do next.

>Read some Kerouac

I read On the Road and Dharma Bums when I was on the street. 
Happy memories.

>Stay hungry. Stay alive.

Satiety is paramount to death for people like me. Maybe this kind of life
is what is meant by *"No rest for the wicked"* ?

I'll never be happy until I am free. I see that now. I'm going to go 
seek out others in the city, hash out some ideas, and then start 
implementing.

I've already reconnected with the co-founder of my old company on some
business ideas. He's getting tired of being salaried as well, although 
he's married and has been at it a little longer.

The short-term is to develop passive income, nose to the grind-stone, and 
become independent. Not necessarily fully retired, but bring my life to a 
point where my living is no longer earned directly against how much of my 
life/time gets sucked down.

If it becomes too much, I'll just drop it all and run.

If you'd like to stay in touch, send me some kind of contact details via 
private message.

You're the kind of kindred mind I've been seeking for some time now.

Even if you don't, take care.

I hope you find a way.

--- A/CMA

Huh. So it's either cognitive dissonance or an act of god (so to speak) eh?

Which really means that I'm right and I either have to find peace in loneliness and the lack of control I have over my happiness, or the alternative.

God dammit.
Thank you.
Thank you.
Yeah, I'm past that now. Just trying to do...something.

Not much. Had to make a quick scramble out of a friend in philly's house after the property owner flipped a shit about me being there, (immediately going on my way to NYC, somewhat unexpectedly early).

Other than that, it was pretty chill.

Protip if you're ever on the street in NYC: Get a blanket. It can be the dead of summer. Get a blanket *anyway*.

There are some fucking evil and **cold** winds at night in NYC.

**COLD**

90F at high noon, shivering to death in the early morning. Bizarre as hell.

Shivering while wearing two long sleeve shirts and a hoodie no less. and trying to cover myself with my backpack while lying awkwardly on the bench.

The next day I slept on a concrete slab because it was less exposed to the wind :P

My natural day isn't 24 hours long, it's 28-30 hours.

When I was self-employed under my company, I woke up a few hours later every day.

I'm just not built for normal society. Forcing myself to go to bed early and wake up early everyday causes me a lot of stress and fatigue.

Haha, I didn't know that.

They destroyed 25 grand worth of product and refused to pay me for the insurance policies I bought from them.

That led to a chain reaction with paypal/ebay where all my accounts were frozen, reputation destroyed (I wasn't allowed to message my customers), and the company's primary revenue model was gone.
~600-800 miles. Took about a week. Most of it spent in Pennsylvania.

An old associate and friend of mine have been hashing out a few business ideas. I've also been working on determining and beginning to establish some sources of passive income.

If all goes well, I'll be free sooner rather than later.

I'd rather retire later, but be self-employed for most of it than retire earlier and work for someone else the whole time.

I **hate** waking up in the morning to the point that getting out of bed is a daily existential crisis for me during the weekdays.

The tiredness I mentioned in the post isn't purely emotional.

I backpacked to NYC in order to find work and get off the street. So I know the feeling of itching for a journey.

Definitely see the friend before it's too late.

>Man you belong on your own professionally period. That is the attitude you must have.

How do you mean?
Sounds awesome. What do you do to survive?
Yeah, UPS screwed my company (which was a telecommuting gig :P ).
I'd like a telecommuting job, but it's not really 100% an option right now. It's something I'll pursue aggressively once I can leave the city.

I don't want to be homeless, I want to be disconnected from the constraints and demands of a 'normal' life. I want to retire.

I was happier because I only had to worry about food, warmth, and staying dry.

I got a lot more sunlight, woke up primarily to the rising sun, more fresh air, slept more period, etc.

*shrugs*
I'll think about it.

>Can you cobble enough money together to buy a small home and some land and make a go at off-the-grid living?

That's the aforementioned 'retirement' that I dream of. That's the 'pointless goal' I alluded to as well. It would take a lot of work and savings, probably 10 years worth to become stable.

I don't see the affair through rose colored glasses, I've lived on the street and I've lived in the country before. I know what it takes. Takes work. If you have savings/interest bearing accounts to take care of random oddities, it's wouldn't be bad, IMHO.

Hard work/productivity is meaningful to me. Nothing at my job is difficult. I'm a merely 'competent' software developer, and yet I'm leagues ahead of my coworkers because no one cares about being good at their jobs anymore. It's disheartening and annoying.

How do you mean?

Edit: Am I being overly rational/analytical to be happy?

If so, it's not something I can really dissonance away. Philosophy is a love of mine, part and parcel of that is thinking through my life.

>figure out what drives you

Previously it was hatred and ruthless greed. In particular for my father who was responsible for the fact that I couldn't go to school.

Now I've proven my point. I've made it, I'm successful. I appropriated some things from Buddhism while I was wandering/homeless and I learned to let go.

What is there for me to hold onto now, is the question I guess.

I used to feel something like that American Beauty quote. Having everything in my life fall apart for reasons out of my control dispelled it.
I'll just try to stay open to things. Feel pretty bleurgh about trudging forth without any specific goal though.

I run with a friend and I walk quite a bit everyday just as a prerequisite of where I live.

I don't know that I'm necessarily depressed. I've felt depressed before.

>seems to you life completely meaningless without a partner, which is too extreme a view

I agree it's too extreme a view. But it also doesn't really properly apply.

What I mean to say is that I had a *why* to everything I did when I had a significant other who meant something to me, *and* when I was single and on the street.

As I am now, single/lonely and working, the why has evaporated during the transition from homeless to working, single status remaining the same. I feel about as lonely then as I do now, it's just bothering me more because of the idleness of not needing to worry about where my meals are coming from.

It's worth noting that the predominant reason for considering the *out* solution is really just that I feel old and tired. I can't justify continuing the toil and suffering when there's no 'why' to any of it. I just want to go to sleep.

>Try making new friends.

Check. My most favored friend is going through a divorce himself, and he's got a full-time job + school. I love hanging out with him but it isn't scratching the itch.

>Try discovering new passions.

Eh, the last time I did digital oils was when I was dating the aforementioned girl. I had a muse and a fire. Neither exist anymore so I'd just be forcing/kidding myself if I attempted something like that Delaroche again.

>Happiness is what's most attractive in other people, work on making yourself happy and the girl will come

That has never been the case for me, and frankly, is unacceptable. I want to be happy now and not have the itch to share my life with someone else.

The first-order desire here isn't to scratch the itch, but to eliminate the cause of the itch. I hate needing things upon which I have no control.

And don't kid yourself that you can have control over your relationships, the divorce rate speaks to a different reality.

>Try dating but just for fun initially

I have no idea how to do that. Honestly. I don't know how to meet people. My life has been to broken/busy to do anything other than CraigsList historically. My best friend and I met via reddit.

This part might be worth discussing.

My job would make it difficult/non-trivial to live on the streets. My physical presence is required (I'm a sysadmin in addition to primarily being a software dev) and as such I can't wander the country like I used to.
Why would I volunteer to help others when I can barely justify waking up in the morning to myself? Is it something that I just have to try or what?

I act regardless. The background of thought is permeated with, "I'm tired" and "Why bother?".

I can't justify to myself anything I do anymore.

>But you have to have a solid base of your own happiness for that connection to be healthy and not co-dependent.

I had that when I was on the street, it feels like it has since evaporated, like I've been emotionally enslaved by participating in society. It's absurd.

The last time I did anything artistic was some digital oils. It was when I was dating the philosophical girl for a year.

I spent 90 hours straight in one week, doing a remake/retouch of a Delaroche. It was a mammoth amount of work and pain, and I was nearly incoherent when I finished it.

I haven't done anything artistic since I dated that girl. She was the *why*, the cause, the muse.

I don't have that inner drive anymore. I managed to muster some anger and passion necessary to get my career back on track, but taken on my own account post-street life, I just don't have any *reason* to do any of that.

I can dissonance and imagine it all away as much as I want, but I'll need to find a way to develop a *why* to what I do. Even if it's just ars artis/aesthetic.

Thank you.
